reasoning_trace.value: The paper presents a frequency-comb-steered ultrawideband quasi-true-time-delay (TTD) beamformer for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). The system uses a dual-comb heterodyne mixing scheme to generate microwave signals that feed a 16-element linear or 4x4 planar antenna array. The beamformer achieves squint-free beamforming across the entire Ku band (12-18 GHz) and demonstrates continuous beam steering with a step of 1 degree. The system also shows integrated ISAR imaging and communication capabilities with a resolution of 2.6 x 3.0 cm and a data rate of 4.8 Gbps.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The system mechanism is based on a photonically steered frequency-diverse array, which uses a dual-comb heterodyne mixing scheme to generate microwave signals. The ISAC coupling mode is achieved through a constant-envelope linear frequency modulation with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CE-LFM-OFDM) waveform, which combines the benefits of LFM and OFDM for both sensing and communication.
